summary: A 1958 R-6 flat cab on a 20-foot timber tower in Idaho's St. Joe National Forest, last staffed full time in 1972; now holds radio and solar gear.

facts.design: 20-ft treated timber tower with R-6 flat cab

access.note: No public access rule found. An OHV route listing allows vehicles and foot traffic, a 2024 visitor found the gate open, and the bottom stairs have been removed.

visit.trail_note: OuterSpatial lists the route as open to motor vehicles, bicycles, horses and pedestrians. A 2024 visitor had been told the gate was always locked but found it open; the bottom set of stairs has been removed.

corrections.why: Idaho Fire Lookouts says the tower has not been staffed since the 1970s, Forest Lookouts says the last full-time staffing was 1972, and the register says it no longer appears to be used as a lookout.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: 1932 is the first pole tower on the site and 1958 is the current R-6 cab. The register records the 1958 cab; firelookout.com describes the earlier tower.

sources.title: The Last Lookout on Dunn Peak

notes_for_editor: Access level 'restricted' is my reading of conflicting evidence: an OHV route listing allows vehicles, and a 2024 visit found the gate open despite reports that it is locked. No official Forest Service access statement was found. Idaho Fire Lookouts gives the 1958 cab as '40 R-6', which looks like a typo for 20 ft; firelookout.com and Forest Lookouts give 20 ft. Forest Lookouts cites Kresek (1932 and 1958 dimensions) but that book was not read. The Trailforks page returned HTTP 403 and was not used. No new photos. The story no longer advises against climbing the tower: the sources say the bottom stairs were removed and the tower is unstaffed, and the story says no official rule was found.
